clue.text: Dull pro with crew troubled celeb, perhaps

indicators.note: something troubled is stirred up and disordered, so the letters before it are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of dull, pro and crew together

explanation.surface: A boring professional and a shaky film crew make a celebrity look bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like a link but simply joins the second batch of anagram letters to the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity is one example of someone who draws large audiences, hence the question-style 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Religious follower elevated an authority

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the words up means reading them from bottom to top

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, a
a tsar is an official with sweeping powers, as in a drugs tsar

explanation.surface: A devout believer has been promoted into a position of power.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rasta, short for Rastafarian, follows the Jamaican religious movement that reveres Haile Selassie.

clue.text: Conflict with Scottish place? It has a castle

parts.note: war is armed conflict
Wick is a town in Caithness in the far north of Scotland

explanation.surface: A battle at a Scottish spot raises the question of a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the English county town, not anywhere Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: Warwick is an English town in the Midlands whose medieval castle is one of the best known in Britain.

clue.text: Exotic root in a lot of Italian food supplying dish

indicators.note: in puts the reshuffled letters inside the shortened Italian food
a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: pasta is the classic Italian staple

indicators.note: something exotic is strange and unfamiliar, so the letters take an unfamiliar order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: An unusual root vegetable mixed into pasta makes a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot roast is a joint of meat slowly braised in a covered pot, served as a main dish.

clue.text: Room in school of theology

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the following run of words

parts.note: spanning the end of school, all of of, and the start of theology

explanation.surface: A room inside a theological college.
explanation.definitionFit: A loft is a room or space under the roof of a house, used for storage or living.

clue.text: Relative with a hint in East End to get another commercial outing?

indicators.note: Cockney speech of London's East End famously drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: REL is a standard abbreviation for relative
taken as written
a hunch is an intuition or hint

explanation.surface: A relative with a tip from London's East End sets out to try business again.
explanation.walkthrough: East End Londoners (Cockneys) traditionally drop their aitches, so the word for hint loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To relaunch a product is to put it back on the market, giving it a further commercial outing.

clue.text: Queen caught sign above Greek port avoiding sun

indicators.note: avoiding the sun means doing without the abbreviation S, so that letter is dropped from the port

parts.note: c is cricket shorthand for caught
Leo is a sign of the zodiac
Patras is a port in the western Peloponnese

explanation.surface: A queen is seized on a Greek waterfront, keeping out of the sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'above' simply places one piece before the next in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was the last ruling queen of Ptolemaic Egypt, famous through Shakespeare and Hollywood.

clue.text: A bloke inhibiting others with a reformist approach?

indicators.note: to inhibit is to hold in or restrain, so the word for others is held within

parts.note: a as in 'a pound a head', meaning per
an oik is a crude or uncouth bloke
taken as written
the others are the rest

explanation.surface: One man holds back everyone else with his zeal for change.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening A stands for per, as in 'ten pounds a day'; 'oik' is British slang for a boorish lout.
explanation.definitionFit: Perestroika was Gorbachev's programme of restructuring the Soviet economy and politics in the 1980s, a reforming policy.

clue.text: Girl in boots getting stripped

indicators.note: stripping takes off the outer covering, so the first and last letters of the word for footwear go

parts.note: wellies are rubber wellington boots

explanation.surface: A girl in her boots is having them taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: Wellies, short for wellingtons, are the British name for rubber rain boots; losing W and S leaves ELLIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellie is a common female first name, and crosswords freely use any girl's name for 'girl'.

clue.text: Artificial sports surface for a trust vandalised

indicators.note: vandalised things are smashed and wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A sports trust's synthetic pitch has been damaged by vandals.
explanation.definitionFit: AstroTurf is the brand name of synthetic grass used for pitches, now a generic term for such playing surfaces.

clue.text: Something thorny in start of golf before lines are broadcast?

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so the words are to be judged by their sound

parts.note: each hole in golf starts from the tee
lines as in rows of seats or plants

explanation.surface: A golfer at the first tee hears a list of lines read out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply puts the tee ahead of the lines; 'start of golf' is a whole phrase meaning the tee, not the letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea rose is a garden rose variety, and like all roses its stems carry thorns.

clue.text: A fool blocks a rabble confronting a province

indicators.note: to block something is to sit in the middle of it, so the fool goes inside the rabble

parts.note: a rabble is an unruly mob
taken as written
taken as written
a nit is a silly person

explanation.surface: An idiot stands in the way of an angry crowd in a Canadian province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confronting' means standing in front of, so the walled-in rabble comes before the last A.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitoba is one of Canada's ten provinces, lying between Saskatchewan and Ontario.

clue.text: Philosopher, Greek character with central point heading off into country

indicators.note: into puts the preceding letters inside the name of the country

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: with its head off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
the navel is the middle point of the body, or the centre of anything

explanation.surface: A Greek thinker heads abroad, taking his main argument with him.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Machiavelli was the Florentine political thinker whose book The Prince makes him a classic political philosopher.

clue.text: A non-drinker standing over short glass depleted in bash

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
TT stands for teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol
a glass that has been drained is empty

explanation.surface: A teetotaller stands over an emptied glass after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing over' places the first pieces above the rest in this down answer; 'bash' is the definition, not a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a bash at something is informal British for having a go, a try or an effort.

clue.text: Negotiate a new section in pamphlet

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the word for a pamphlet

parts.note: a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political
taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new
S abbreviates section, as in legal references

explanation.surface: Someone discusses adding a new part to a leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact business is to carry it through or conduct a deal, close in sense to negotiating terms.

clue.text: Constant request for drink container

parts.note: c is the scientific symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: Someone keeps asking for something to drink from.
explanation.definitionFit: A cask is a wooden barrel used for storing wine, beer or spirits.

clue.text: Figure pruned plant lining one road

indicators.note: a lining surrounds what it encloses, so the plant wraps around the next pieces
pruning trims the end off, so the plant loses its final letter

parts.note: statice is sea lavender, a flowering plant
the Roman numeral for one
ST abbreviates street, a road

explanation.surface: A trimmed shrub edges a single road.
explanation.walkthrough: Statice, also called sea lavender, is a flower often dried for arrangements.
explanation.definitionFit: A statistic is a number or figure derived from data, such as an average or percentage.

clue.text: Bird, maybe, showing exaggeration?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: bird is slang for a prison sentence
second meaning: a claim that goes beyond the truth

explanation.surface: A bird puffing itself up looks like exaggeration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' here is British slang for time in prison (from rhyming slang 'birdlime', time), not a feathered creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch is both slang for a jail term and something that strains the truth, as in 'that's a bit of a stretch'.

clue.text: US city in due course imprisoning criminal gained

indicators.note: imprisoning locks the jumbled letters inside the short word for in due course

parts.note: so in the sense of then or consequently, as in 'and so it came about'

indicators.note: criminal suggests being bent or crooked, so these letters are bent out of order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: An American city eventually jails a crook who profited.
explanation.definitionFit: San Diego is a large Californian city on the Pacific coast near the Mexican border.

clue.text: Source of messages detaining tense palace official

indicators.note: detaining someone holds them inside, so the source of messages holds the letter for tense

parts.note: a courier delivers messages and parcels
T abbreviates tense in grammar

explanation.surface: A messenger is holding a nervous royal attendant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' reads as nervous, but it is the grammatical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtier is an attendant at a royal court, an official of the palace household.

clue.text: Garment Gershwin's put back

indicators.note: putting something back sends it the other way, so the name is read from its end

parts.note: Ira Gershwin, lyricist brother of George; possessive gives the S

explanation.surface: A garment belonging to Gershwin has been put away again.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gershwin meant is Ira, the lyricist, not George.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is the long draped cloth garment worn by women in South Asia.

clue.text: Chap in ground after sandwich initially and green stuff?

indicators.note: initially points to just the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: its opening letter

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken down, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters of chap and in

explanation.surface: A man on the ground after a sandwich and some greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the anagram after the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green vegetable, hence green stuff with a playful question mark.

clue.text: Pain with gut fooling around college — like a miscreant?

indicators.note: around puts the jumbled letters on either side of the abbreviation for college
fooling about means messing around, so these letters are messed into a new order

parts.note: the letters of pain and gut together
C abbreviates college

explanation.surface: A student with stomach ache messes about on campus, behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two words of anagram letters rather than acting as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting up means misbehaving, which is how a wrongdoer or naughty child carries on.

clue.text: Two wrongs found with a Mexican food

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
an ill is a harm or wrong
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two mistakes are discovered in a Mexican dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two wrongs' supplies two separate words for a wrong, placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is the thin flatbread of maize or wheat that is a staple of Mexican cooking.

clue.text: Liberal school revealed

parts.note: L abbreviates Liberal
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A progressive school has been exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College near Windsor is Britain's best-known private boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is to disclose a secret, so 'let on' in the past tense matches revealed.

clue.text: Northern clubs, maybe, in middle of week getting bathroom

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the central pair from the week
the middle of a four-letter word is its two central letters

parts.note: the two central letters of the word
N abbreviates northern
clubs is one example of a suit of cards

explanation.surface: Northern clubs midweek get a new bathroom fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' tempts toward golf or night clubs, but it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: An en suite is a bathroom attached directly to a bedroom; the term is used as a noun in British estate-agent speak.

clue.text: Comfort and support for artist left out

indicators.note: left out means the abbreviation for left is omitted

parts.note: an easel holds a painter's canvas
L abbreviates left

explanation.surface: A neglected artist needs comfort and support.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is a state of comfort and freedom from pain or worry.

clue.text: A post in TA devised? It's a starter

indicators.note: something devised is worked out or invented, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: the letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A role is created in the Territorial Army, perhaps as a first step.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force, but here it is just two anagram letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian first course of cold meats, olives and vegetables served before the main meal.

clue.text: Psychiatrist at home probing convict

indicators.note: a probe goes inside something, so the phrase for home pushes into the word for convict

parts.note: an old lag is a seasoned convict
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist at home examines a prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lag' is British slang for a prisoner, usually an old lag.
explanation.definitionFit: R. D. Laing was a Scottish psychiatrist famous for his radical writings on mental illness in the 1960s.

clue.text: Dominating all else is ranch with grove I cultivated

indicators.note: cultivated ground is dug and turned over, so the letters are turned over into a new order

parts.note: the letters of ranch, grove and I

explanation.surface: A farm with a tended orchard dominates the landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overarching covers or governs everything else, like an arch spanning all beneath it.
